title: Sweep the last retired delivery-rule statements out of docs, skills and README
action: An independent review of the hps-2 and hps-4 docs commits found retired rules still stated as live in six places, plus two precision defects. hps-3 and hps-6 have landed by the time this cell runs, so the delivery shape the docs must describe is the FINAL one — read `deliver_pointer` and `render_brief` in the worktree and describe what they actually do, never this list alone. As of hps-6 that shape is: the brief's first instruction tells the worker to write `ack-<round>.json` atomically; the pointer is submitted ONCE through `herdr agent prompt --wait --until working --timeout`; delivery is confirmed by the worker's ack file appearing, or the round's result file for an ultra-fast round; a `blocked` pane and herdr's `agent_prompt_stalled` end the wait at once; and the pointer is RESENT only when the agent has gone back to idle or done with still no ack — never on a timer while it is working. Fix each finding: (a) `handing-a-foreign-agent-its-brief.md` around lines 107-110 still says the pointer 'is re-sent a fixed number of times, each attempt polling for the ack'. Wrong on both halves — replace with the shape above and cite herding-prompt-stall D1 and D4. (b) Same file, around line 143: the pointer list still names a 'resend ceiling' in `herding/run.rs`; name the delivery path, the ack-wait budget and the stall/blocked errors instead. (c) Same file, frontmatter around lines 4 and 11-12: the `description` still carries the retired rule verbatim ('only a state transition the agent itself caused counts as evidence it received anything'), `sources` does not list `docs/history/herding-prompt-stall/CONTEXT.md`, and `decisions` still lists `herding-prompt-verify D1 (bounded resends...)` and `herding-run-ready-wait D1 (readiness is observed before the send)` with no narrowing note. Fix the frontmatter, then REGENERATE the area index rather than hand-editing `docs/knowledge/areas/bee-herding/index.md` — its line 14 mirrors the description and is generated from it. (d) `the-run-verb-and-worker-outcomes.md` around line 83 keeps 'the state-receipt delivery' as a live term; rename it to the pointer-delivery path and cite D1/D4. (e) `skills/bee-herding/references/operational-invariants.md` around lines 248-275 frames delivery entirely as lifecycle state ('Readiness and delivery both defer to herdr's own lifecycle contract', 'The send is now herdr's own atomic submit-and-observe'). Keep the D1 stall and D3 blocked detectors, but state the receipt itself is D4's ack file and that lifecycle state is a FAILURE detector only — today this file and the sibling knowledge page contradict each other. (f) `README.md` around line 412: the flow diagram states all three retired rules at once ('delivered only when the agent's STATE says so — status flips to working/done or the result file appears; still idle -> resend, bounded'). Rewrite to the ack-or-result receipt with the stall and blocked failures. (g) PRECISION, two places. `agent-resolution-and-spawn-commands.md` around line 144 says 'Five states' and enumerates `working` as if quoted from herdr; the quoted contract names four (`idle`, `done`, `blocked`, `unknown`) and mentions `working` only as 'a non-working state' — say so honestly. And in that file around lines 150-151 and in `operational-invariants.md` around lines 254-255, 'only ever reads over the CLI, which never marks a tab seen' overstates the contract: a focus command is also CLI and DOES mark a tab seen; only CLI reads do not. Use the phrasing the sibling page already gets right: 'CLI reads never mark a tab seen'. (h) In `handing-a-foreign-agent-its-brief.md`, citations degrade to bare `(D4)`, `(D2)`, `(D1)`, `(D3)` after the first full one; give the full feature-qualified id on first use in each section. Do not restructure or renumber any document, and do not touch the `herding.agents` registry sections.
